mission.display_title: Construct a prediction interval for a future observation
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to construct a prediction interval for a future observation based on a model fitted to a random sample — so prediction is distinct from parameter CI — without pretending given-sampling-distribution CIs (3.2.3) are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to target a future observation with a prediction interval and refuse collapsing it into yesterday's parameter CI.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from a fitted model on a random sample to a prediction interval for a future observation.
mission.learning_objective: Prediction interval for a future observation based on a model fitted to a random sample.
mission.concept_focus: Fitted model → future observation → prediction interval → refuse given-distribution CI-as-done.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you constructed a parameter confidence interval (3.2.1). Today continues topic 3.2 at LO 3.2.2 — prediction intervals.
mission.why_now: 3.2.2 is contiguous after parameter CI. Closing it prevents a cliff at prediction while keeping given-sampling-distribution CI as day three.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to construct a prediction interval for a future observation and distinguish it from a parameter CI.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Lambda Day 2 because Continuity Front membership places prediction immediately after parameter CI.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What does a prediction interval claim about a future observation? (2) What role does a model fitted to a random sample play? (3) Name one difference from a parameter confidence interval.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: A prediction interval targets a future observation (not the parameter itself), using a model fitted to a random sample. A parameter CI targets the unknown parameter — different object.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You fit a model to historical annual losses and need an interval for next year's loss Y_new. (1) What does a prediction interval cover that a parameter CI for E[Y] does not? (2) Refuse: 'My confidence interval for the mean loss already finished the prediction-interval LO.'
knowledge_checks.body: Prediction interval for a future observation; refuse parameter-CI conflation.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Prediction intervals cover future data; parameter CIs cover parameters.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) A prediction interval aims to cover a future observation Y_new (parameter uncertainty plus process/residual variation); a parameter CI covers only a fixed unknown parameter such as E[Y]. (2) Refuse: a parameter CI is not a prediction interval — different target, typically wider for prediction.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating a CI for the mean as interchangeable with a prediction interval for a new observation.
success_criteria: States that prediction covers a future observation (beyond a mean parameter).
Refuses treating a parameter CI as finishing prediction.
